maria: FYI - after the KMS rotation at ~03:02 UTC we're seeing a surge of SCIM deprovision failures for Google Workspace users. Logs show JWE/SAML decrypt errors. sample:
```
ERROR: jwe_decrypt: kid not found (alias=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/idp/cryptoKeys/rdw-idp-v2)
TRACE: saml: decrypt assertion failed: RSA_OAEP padding error
SCIM: deprov failed user=alice@example.com msg=decryption_failed
```
Anyone with quick ideas? identity-bot: automated note — kms.rotate triggered by ops@redwood 2026-03-20T03:02:14Z (rotation-id: rot-20260320-03). ajay: can you paste the full trace id from the proxy logs? need to correlate with KMS audit. maria: trace=3f4a9c7b, pulled proxied logs and stack: ```2026-03-20T03:02:15Z proxy[svc-idp] trace=3f4a9c7b JWE header=kid:rdw-idp-v2 alg:RSA-OAEP-256
2026-03-20T03:02:15Z kms-client trace=3f4a9c7b getKeyVersion alias=rdw-idp-v3 -> success
2026-03-20T03:02:15Z proxy trace=3f4a9c7b decrypt error: KMS.Decrypt failed: rpc error: code=NotFound
```
sam: preliminary thought — looks like the SP (our SAML proxy) is still emitting kid=rdw-idp-v2 while the KMS alias was repointed to rdw-idp-v3. If the key id changed and versions were removed, KMS would return NotFound for the old kid. also alg mismatch note — OAEP-256 vs OAEP. elin: also see SCIM backlog showing repeated requeue attempts; that can create duplicate role rows when downstream succeeded partially. ajay: pinging cloud-kms to verify alias -> key binding history. can we extract the JWE header for a failing assertion? maria: pasted one above. ajay: thx. quick check: rdw-idp-v2 key version shows disabled and was scheduled for destruction with a policy that removed decrypt permission from our service account — that would explain NotFound. sam: two prongs — fix KMS mapping (rebind alias or re-enable old key temporarily) and reprocess SCIM queue. need to confirm whether any assertions were re-signed with new kid before consumers updated. maria: agree. plan proposal: 1) rebind alias to point back to v2 for a short window (owner: ajay) 2) re-enable decrypt permission for service account or add fallback key policy (owner: cloud-kms) 3) reprocess SCIM retry queue and watch duplicates (owner: maria) 4) add a preflight check in deployment pipeline to validate JWE.kid exists in KMS before rotate (owner: sam) 5) create saved audit search for KMS key alias rebind events (owner: ajay).
identity-bot: queued reprocess job id=job-7721 scheduled by maria. sam: when reprocessing, add normalization step to dedupe by externalId to avoid role duplicates. elin: started a small run — reprocess cleared ~40 users, 80 left. seeing 2 users with duplicate role mapping that need manual cleanup. ajay: cloud-kms confirmed alias swap happened as part of rotation but the automation removed the previous key version prematurely; team is re-adding alias pointer now. maria: doing a quick smoke test against staging SAML proxy — using a signed+encrypted assertion with kid=rdw-idp-v2 decrypts successfully once alias is pointed back. sam: we should also check the assertion encryption alg; some clients still emit RSA-OAEP but KMS free-form expects RSA-OAEP-256. failing mismatch shows as padding error. ajay: noted — will add alg compatibility check to rollout doc. elin: manual cleanup script ran and fixed 2 dup role rows, will hand off to customer-succ for outreach for edge cases. maria: raising a postmortem and will include timeline and suggested mitigations (alias staging, preflight, alerting). ajay: opening compliance ticket and adding a saved query: "kms.alias_churn where service_account=svc-idp". sam: also adding an alert: if jwe_decrypt NotFound spikes > 5/minute trigger pager. maria: TL;DR root cause = alias repointed + old key version disabled before consumers rotated -> JWE kid mismatch + alg mismatch for some clients; remediation = rebind alias + reprocess + manual cleanup for two users. will update when backlog is zero. :white_check_mark:
